You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to buy or auction Virginia Avenue.

I own St. Charles Place in the pink group, so Virginia Avenue would complete it. I have $160 cash and several mortgaged properties.

States Avenue is owned by p1 and mortgaged, so buying Virginia would not complete the pink group. I would spend all $160 cash. My strategy prioritizes dark blue properties.

I rolled doubles and must roll again. With zero cash, I would be bankrupt if I land on rent property. Building Park Place to three houses would cost $200.

I could sell houses on Boardwalk or Park Place to raise cash if I land on rent. Auctioning Virginia Avenue might let p1 bid for it and complete the pink group.

I should not spend my last $160 on Virginia Avenue. Auctioning it would not threaten me, since p4 has no pink properties and p1 still needs St. Charles to complete the group.

I will start an auction for Virginia Avenue. I must avoid selling Boardwalk houses, since that would drop the kill rent to $600.

I should not appear desperate. I will keep Virginia unowned or in weak hands. If p1 acquires it, they still need St. Charles to complete the pink group. They may pressure me for a trade. I already rejected offers that unblock monopolies.

I will auction Virginia Avenue to preserve my cash. I do not need the pink group; dark blue is my priority. p4 has $940 and four houses on Mediterranean and Baltic, so those spaces are dangerous if I land there.

I am calculating the next roll from Virginia Avenue. The spaces ahead include St. James Place, Tennessee Avenue, New York Avenue, and Kentucky Avenue. p3 owns all three orange properties with one house each. I am checking standard rent values for these houses to assess the risk of landing there.

Orange rent values with one house are $70 on Tennessee and $80 on New York. I could survive those with my full cash balance. St. James Place unimproved would charge $28 under monopoly rules. Selling one Boardwalk house would return $100, but that would drop the kill rent from $1400 to $600. I am also checking red properties like Kentucky and Illinois, which have two houses and would cost $500 or $600.

The next roll from Virginia Avenue would hit St. James Place for $28, Tennessee Avenue for $70, New York Avenue for $80, and either Kentucky or Indiana for $250. Illinois would cost $300. The B&O Railroad is mortgaged and would not charge rent.

I cannot afford the $250 rent on Kentucky Avenue with only $160 cash. I will keep that cash and auction Virginia Avenue instead. Buying it would leave me owning two pinks while St. Charles Place remains mortgaged, so I could not build until unmortgaging. I will avoid revealing my strategy in the public message.
